subject: Cache + batching sensitivity probe — next steps and test plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Cache + batching sensitivity probe — next steps and test plan

Alex — great conversation today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap (call highlights):
- AcmeCloud: primary use is text classification + summarization at 200k–1M tokens/day, p95 latency target 250ms for single-turn inference.
- Main question: cost sensitivity to batching and KV/prefix caching; how much infra delta vs Bedrock/Vertex AI when cache hit rate moves from 30% to 80%.
- Security + contract: standard cloud SOC2 ok, procurement lead is Priya Shah (cc’d).

Proposed probe (what Redwood will run):
1) Baseline: Hosted API on model-alpha (FP16) — run synthetic workload of 1M tokens to measure per-1M token cost, p50/p95 latency, and memory.
2) Cache sensitivity runs: same 1M token batch with simulated prefix reuse at 30%, 50%, 80% cache hit rates. Capture token-level cost and KV hit rate.
3) Batching sweep: payload concurrency 1–32, measure throughput and p95 latency; test batch sizes expected in your traffic (avg len ~120 tokens).
4) Hyperscaler comparison: replicate identical workload against Bedrock (ml-infer-v2) and Vertex AI (inference-v1) using our standard config; measure per-1M token unit cost normalized to same instance types where possible.

Deliverables (48–72 hrs after test start):
- PDF recap with per-1M token cost breakdown (token compute, I/O, fixed infra), p50/p95 latency tables, and sensitivity plots.
- CSV with raw logs and aggregated metrics.
- Short recommendation: conservative estimate for production (cost range + suggested cache/batching knobs).

Ask from AcmeCloud to proceed:
- Confirm permission to run the hyperscaler replicates (we will only use your anonymized sample prompts and synthetic traffic)
- Preferred window for the 1M token probe (we recommend a low-traffic overnight window to avoid interference)

I attached a short runner (redwood-econ-run.pdf) and a test spec CSV (cache-batch-test-specs.csv) with the exact parameters we’ll use.

Next step: can you confirm Priya is the procurement contact and give us a 2-hr window this week to kick off? If yes, Ben will schedule the runs and share the results.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-econ-run.pdf (summary), cache-batch-test-specs.csv (test matrix)

Thanks Rishi — useful recap. Priya is our procurement lead and ok for the probe; Priya, I’ve flagged this with Rishi’s team.

A couple of notes from our side:
- We can provide a 1M-token anonymized sample set (redacted PII) and two short real-traffic windows: Thu 09/16 23:00–01:00 PT and Sat 09/18 01:00–03:00 PT. Thu works better for us.
- We are particularly interested in: (a) cost delta when cache hit moves from ~35% (our baseline) to >70% and (b) how batching affects tail latencies for short prompts (~60 tokens).
- Procurement/legal: we’ll need a short one-page MSA addendum for the probe (we can sign an NDA amendment if needed).

Happy to run the first window Thu night. Please confirm final test times and we’ll stand up sample telemetry access.

Operational checklist:
- We will run three cache profiles in sequence (30%, 50%, 80% simulated hit) using your sample set; each profile ~333k tokens to total ~1M.
- Batching sweep: concurrency {1,2,4,8,16,32} with a 60s warm-up and 5m steady collection; target p95 accuracy ±5%.
- Hyperscaler runs: we will spin equivalent configs and flag any SKU mismatches; costs will be normalized to token/time basis and annotated with instance SKU.
- Measurement: per-1M token cost (USD), p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit ratio.

Pre-test ask (from our side):
1) Confirm the anonymized sample set is available by Wed EOD PST.
2) Provide contact for any network whitelisting if we need to hit internal endpoints — otherwise we’ll use your public telemetry endpoints.

I’ll provision the test harness tonight and send a run link (and a single-use debug key) to Priya and Alex. We will not retain raw prompt text beyond the duration of the probe; logs will be redacted per the MSA addendum.

—Ben
